title: Starry La Silla
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Stars wheel around the southern celestial pole through a night at ESO's La Silla Observatory in northern Chile. The fuzzy sections in the trails on the right come from the Magellanic Clouds, two small galaxies that neighbor the Milky Way.

The dome in the picture houses ESO's 3.6-meter telescope and HARPS, the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher, which ESO calls the world's foremost exoplanet hunter. In the lower right, a rectangular building holds the 0.25-meter TAROT telescope, designed to respond fast whenever a gamma-ray burst is spotted.

La Silla was ESO's first observing site and is still among the leading observatories of the southern hemisphere. Beyond the 3.6-meter, it hosts the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope and the New Technology Telescope, whose mirror is 3.58 meters across. The NTT was the first telescope to use active optics, making it the forerunner of every large modern telescope.

understand.summary: This is a star-trail photograph by Iztok Bončina, recording the stars' motion over the night. The source does not publish camera or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. The trails build up only because the camera recorded Earth's rotation over time.
